oewn-00701392-v.learner: to make up your mind about something.
examples: if I should resolve to quit Netherfield, I should probably be off in five minutes
But he found Lydia absolutely resolved on remaining where she was.

oewn-01023429-v.learner: to come to a conclusion after talking something over or thinking it through.
examples: After a long meeting the members resolved that the old rule should stand.

oewn-00700621-v.learner: to bring something to an end by settling it for good.
examples: The two families asked a judge to resolve the quarrel over the land.

oewn-01779456-v.learner: to be in love with someone.
examples: And do you really love him quite well enough?

oewn-01779085-v.learner: to feel great affection or liking for someone or something.
examples: He loves his grandmother and writes to her every week.
I love walking home in the rain.

oewn-05842164-n.learner: something that is in your mind; the main thing you are thinking about.
examples: the thought will doubtless seem heretical to more than one school of critics

oewn-05778923-n.learner: the work your mind does when you consider something carefully.
examples: After a week of thought, he made up his mind to go.

oewn-05954491-n.learner: something you believe or judge to be so, without proof that it is certain.
examples: What are your thoughts on the new road?

oewn-02092374-v.learner: to move or go along steadily, or little by little.
examples: as the time drew near, she would have been very sorry for any delay

oewn-02298109-v.learner: to get or gain something out of something else.
examples: She drew great comfort from her sister's letters.

oewn-00732743-v.learner: to make or work something out in your mind.
examples: resolving within herself to draw no limits in future to the impudence of an impudent man

oewn-06707972-n.learner: words, or an act, that show praise and admiration.
examples: I did not expect such a compliment.
Accept my thanks for the compliment you are paying me.

oewn-02732039-v.learner: to keep yourself from doing something; this use always has a negative word with it.
examples: I cannot help laughing myself at your surprise to-morrow morning
I cannot help supposing that the hope of revenging himself on me was a strong inducement.

oewn-02553283-v.learner: to give someone help, or to be of service to them.
examples: She helped her mother carry the basket up the stairs.
Making a list helps when you have a lot to remember.
I am not afraid; for though I am the youngest, I'm the tallest.

oewn-00546213-s.learner: full of regret or concern; often used to make an unwelcome thing sound gentler.
examples: I am afraid you do not like your pen.
I am afraid I did not do so much as I might have done.

oewn-00546451-s.learner: feeling worry or concern, or feeling unsure and unsafe.
examples: I am afraid of alarming you
She was afraid that her letter had been read the wrong way.

oewn-07525587-n.learner: the shock you feel when something you did not expect at all happens to you.
examples: Jane looked at Elizabeth with surprise and concern.

oewn-07312772-n.learner: an event that comes all at once and was not expected.
examples: is not this an agreeable surprise?

oewn-00554692-n.learner: the act of catching someone when they are not expecting it.
examples: Compliments always take you by surprise, and me never.
They took the town by surprise before dawn.

oewn-10646084-n.learner: a person with a certain character or nature.
examples: I am in the least unwilling to think her a very good sort of girl
just enough to make one good sort of man

oewn-05847533-n.learner: a group of things that are put together because they share some quality.
examples: She was resolved against any sort of conversation with him

oewn-04753502-n.learner: a rough way of naming something when it is only close to what you call it.
examples: He was wearing a sort of cloak made out of an old blanket.

oewn-05572223-n.learner: the gripping part at the end of your arm.
examples: Elizabeth impatiently caught it from his hand.
She held out her hand: he kissed it with affectionate gallantry

oewn-05861538-n.learner: one of the two sides of a question.
examples: On the other hand, I, for my part, declare for Pride and Prejudice unhesitatingly.

oewn-06415036-n.learner: writing that a person has made by hand.
examples: I knew the letter was hers from the small neat hand.
